Tense. Strategic. Deeply engaging. We build tabletop experiences around tactical positioning, meaningful choices, and direct player interaction — no heads-down solitaire, just sharp tables where smart maneuvers win the day.

Discover Pocket Shoguns Our Design Philosophy

Studio Philosophy

Board games should be tense, highly strategic, and deeply engaging. We design for players who want to out-think each other, not just out-roll the dice.

位置

Tactical positioning

Where you stand on the board matters as much as what's in your hand. Terrain, timing, and formation decide outcomes.

選択

Meaningful choices

Every decision carries real weight and real cost. No filler turns, no choices that don't change the table.

対峙

Direct player interaction

Your opponents are the game. We build systems where players clash, negotiate, and outmaneuver one another directly.

Our Flagship Title

Sengoku Jidai · The Age of the Country at War

Pocket Shoguns

A game of asymmetric power, sequential combat, and the constant tension between ruthless expansion and the Code of Honor.

将

Asymmetric Daimyo Powers

Every Daimyo commands their domain differently. Learn one clan's strengths and you've barely started to understand the table.

陣

Sequential Combat

Battles unfold in ordered strikes, not simultaneous dice-piles. Read your opponent's formation and commit your forces with precision.

図

Dynamic Map Generation

No two campaigns share a battlefield. The map assembles itself each session, so opening strategy is never memorized — it's discovered.

義

The Code of Honor

Expand too ruthlessly and the Code turns against you. Every conquest is weighed against the reputation it costs.

The Daimyō Registry

Thirteen warlords. Thirteen ways to rule.

Expansion
Expansion

From the Rulebook

More than dice and armies.

運命

Destiny Cards

Lose your Daimyō or your castle and you draw a card in return. Fortune favors the desperate — an ambush, a sudden reversal, a second chance.

攻城

No castle falls easy

Defenders inside a castle double their dice. Only artillery can strike inside from outside the walls — everyone else has to break down the gate first.

名誉

Every choice leaves a mark

Sparing an enemy, refusing a duel, burning a castle — honor and dishonor track every decision you make, not just the battles you win.

同盟

Clans take sides

Neutral clans aren't neutral forever — they'll join whoever holds the most honor, the most land, or simply pays the most gold.

南蛮

No port, no powder

Gunpowder came to Japan by sea — Portuguese traders and Nanban ships brought the matchlock to these shores, and in Pocket Shoguns it still arrives that way. Command a port, or fight the old-fashioned way — steel against steel.

誘惑

The Kunoichi's game

She doesn't fight fair. Seduce a Daimyō's movement to a halt, or slip him something fatal — either way, he never saw it coming.

浪人

Legendary Rōnin

Some warriors can't be recruited with gold — only earned through honor. The Legendary Rōnin answers to reputation, not coin.

鬼

The Namahage's roar

Half demon, half folklore, all terror. The Namahage can scare an entire enemy army three tiles back with a scream alone — though even it can't budge Special Units, Ships, Rōnin, or a Daimyō dug into a castle.

恥

What the Ninja costs you

Hiring a Ninja or Kunoichi isn't free in more ways than gold — it costs you Honor the moment you recruit one. Assassination is effective. It's also a stain that follows you.

隠

Vanish into the treeline

Step a Special Unit onto a forest tile and it disappears entirely — untouchable, unkillable, invisible to every eye on the board until it chooses to strike.

兵糧攻め

Siege and starve

Surround a castle and it earns no gold until the siege breaks — but it isn't defenseless. Archers and gunners can fire down fiercely on the besiegers from the walls.

Every unit, hand-sculpted

Castles, ships, siege weapons, and every clan’s warriors — all part of the campaign.

Expansion

Warrior Monks & Mounted Matchlocks

New units ride into the campaign — mounted matchlock riders bring speed and firepower together, warrior monks fight bound by their own code, and two more castle strongholds make six-player campaigns possible.

New to the campaign

Mounted matchlocks, warrior monks, and two more strongholds to claim.
